Layout and Styling

Every UIElement has position, size and color properties. These are used by the window and its containers to calculate where each element is drawn.

Position and Size

  • X / Y: The offset inside the parent's content area. An empty value means 0. The value center can be used to center a position.
  • Width / Height: A number of console cells or a percentage of the available space. Both default to 100%.
  • MinWidth / MaxWidth: The minimum and maximum horizontal size. MinHeight and MaxHeight apply to the vertical size.
  • XYAlignment: The position used to anchor the control, such as TopLeft, BottomLeft or Centered.
  • ActualX / ActualY / ActualWidth / ActualHeight: The calculated position and size after layout.

Percentages are calculated from the space offered by the parent. They do not support expressions such as calc() or 100% - 2.

Creating a Page Layout

MUIPage does not place children below each other automatically. If two children use the same position, they will overlap. You can set X and Y yourself, or use a GridContainer to split the space into cells.

Borders and Content Size

A border uses one cell on each side of a control. This means a bordered TextBox needs 3 rows for one line of input, or 5 rows when it also has a label and separator:

TextAlignment controls the text inside a TextBlock, while XYAlignment controls the position of the whole element. GetAbsolutePosition can be used when you need the position relative to the console rather than the parent.

Colors

  • Foreground / Background: The normal text and background colors. A transparent background preserves what is underneath it.
  • FocusedForeground / FocusedBackground: Colors used by controls for their focused state.
  • BorderColor / FocusedBorderColor: The normal and focused border colors.

MXML colors can be named colors, hex values such as #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB, or comma-separated RGB/ARGB bytes.

Drawing Order

Z controls the drawing order of siblings. Focusing an element does not change that order. Use BringToFront or SendToBack when you need to change which sibling is drawn last.

Text is measured using console cell widths. Combining characters, emoji and other complex text can still depend on the terminal and font being used.
